summary: Static site: Astro (web), hosted on Cloudflare Pages — Cloudflare edge network, at an estimated $0-4/month.

frontend.justification: Team already writes css, html, javascript for the UI; server-rendered/static HTML that search engines index; pre-built static pages, no server needed; good low running cost (priority 5/5); good fast delivery (priority 4/5).

alternatives.why_not: With priorities.time_to_market=4, Astro is faster to deliver with. Known limit of Hugo: go templating is unfamiliar to JS developers.
Needs a server runtime for a site that does not (project.type=content_site); with priorities.cost=5, Astro is cheaper to run. Known limit of SvelteKit: smaller hiring pool than React.

frontend.contrast: Astro (web) rather than Hugo. With priorities.time_to_market=4, Astro is faster to deliver with. Trade-off accepted: Interactive widgets need islands.

backend.justification: No application server is needed: there are no accounts, payments, uploads or dynamic data; pages are pre-built at deploy time.

alternatives.why_not: nothing to compute at request time (requirements.auth is none; no realtime, uploads, multi-tenancy or ML features are requested; requirements.payments is false); add a backend when accounts, stored user data or server-side payments appear
a server to run and pay for with no feature that needs it; add a backend when accounts, stored user data or server-side payments appear

backend.contrast: No backend rather than Netlify/Cloudflare serverless functions. Nothing to compute at request time (requirements.auth is none; no realtime, uploads, multi-tenancy or ML features are requested; requirements.payments is false); add a backend when accounts, stored user data or server-side payments appear.

what_would_change.new_choice: Node.js 24 LTS: Next.js route handlers + server actions (same app as the UI)

database.justification: Content lives as Markdown/HTML files in the repository; there is no user data to store.

alternatives.why_not: no runtime data to persist; add a database when the site starts storing accounts, orders or submissions
a single author edits files directly

database.contrast: No database rather than SQLite. No runtime data to persist; add a database when the site starts storing accounts, orders or submissions.

hosting.justification: A static site needs nothing more than a CDN host; fits a zero budget on its free plan; fully managed runtime (patching, TLS, scaling handled) for a team without a DevOps person; good low running cost (priority 5/5); good fast delivery (priority 4/5).

alternatives.why_not: Close on everything this input rates important; the remaining difference is a low priority (priorities.scalability=1), on which Cloudflare Pages is built to scale further (close call).
With priorities.time_to_market=4, Cloudflare Pages is faster to deliver with. Known limit of Amazon S3 + CloudFront: more setup than a git-push host (bucket policy, distribution, cache invalidation).

tradeoffs: 500 builds/month and 20,000 files per site on Free
No regional pinning of edge-cached content

pareto.note: No eligible option rates at least as well on all six priorities (cost, delivery, scalability, performance, maintainability, security).

alternatives.choice: Amazon S3 + CloudFront (static site) — CloudFront edge (S3 origin bucket in your chosen region)

flip_point.new_choice: Amazon S3 + CloudFront (static site) — CloudFront edge (S3 origin bucket in your chosen region)

confidence.label: low
confidence.basis: stability 0.75 (moderate) over 53 priority vectors; score margin 0.4 over the runner-up (near-tie).

hosting.contrast: Cloudflare Pages rather than Firebase Hosting (Google Cloud). Close on everything this input rates important; the remaining difference is a low priority (priorities.scalability=1), on which Cloudflare Pages is built to scale further (close call). Trade-off accepted: 500 builds/month and 20,000 files per site on Free.

what_would_change.new_choice: Amazon S3 + CloudFront (static site) — CloudFront edge (S3 origin bucket in your chosen region)
Firebase Hosting (Google Cloud) — Firebase global CDN

supporting.justification: The site build runs on every push and a passing build deploys to Cloudflare Pages; the cost band reserves $0-4/month for a team of 1 (planning estimate).

alternatives.why_not: equally capable; for a team of 1 without a DevOps engineer (team.has_devops=false), ready-made GitHub deploy actions for Cloudflare Pages mean less pipeline code to maintain

tradeoffs: Secrets must be stored as encrypted environment secrets

supporting.justification: The owner writes posts in Markdown in the repository; every push rebuilds and publishes the site.

alternatives.why_not: adds accounts and cost for a single author

tradeoffs: Non-technical editors would need a CMS later

assumptions: Hosting Cloudflare Pages: $0-0/month at the 'tiny' tier.
Excluded: taxes, domain names, paid support plans and data-egress spikes. Order-of-magnitude band, not a quote.

warnings.message: The $0 budget is met only on free tiers (estimate $0-4/month): free plans cap requests, bandwidth, build minutes or storage, and the upper bound applies once a cap is passed. Set usage alerts or spend caps and check the plan limits before launch.

assumptions: requirements.p95_latency_ms absent or null: no explicit latency target; typical web latency assumed.
Knowledge base as of 2026-11-11; lifecycle and pricing judgements use that date, not the run date.
Scale tier 'tiny' from 3,000 users and ~50 peak concurrent users (people, not requests per second; used only for sizing and cost).
